decision.note: Priority is inherited from the AI-Ques portfolio entry and is not a repository-quality score.

strengths: P004 is explicitly prototype_only and keeps public character chat conceptually separate from research-side inference.
P005/Future You evidence import is now default-off, requires explicit user opt-in, is withdrawable, and legacy imported influence is removed when consent is absent.
P004 exposes a two-step clear-all control covering module-local localStorage, IndexedDB Skill Vault and the current-tab BYOK key without deleting other P00 modules.
P004 has executable runtime behavior tests for consent, creator validation, memory normalization, safety fallback, BYOK success/HTTP/network paths and key lifecycle.
All observed third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to immutable commit SHAs and the NVWA protocol is pinned to a concrete upstream commit.
Observed user/model rendering paths use textContent; observed innerHTML assignments are fixed templates rather than free model/user text.
BYOK API keys remain current-tab sessionStorage only and the UI discloses browser-side key exposure risk.
The NVWA local fallback remains explicitly labelled a Character Skill draft rather than pretending to be a completed research distillation.
P00 Quality Gate and GitHub Pages deployment both passed on the remediated audited commit.

evidence: P004 README, module manifest and NVWA contract clearly separate character chat, optional distillation, memory, Observer and prototype/non-diagnostic boundaries.
Production-only boundaries such as authenticated admin access remain explicitly distinguished from the static Pages prototype.
Exact-main P00 Quality Gate passed and now runs executable tests/p004-runtime.mjs in addition to syntax and structure checks.
Runtime tests exercise consent, creator-step validation, memory normalization, safety fallback and OpenAI-compatible API success/HTTP/network branches.
Full browser UI flows, real provider calls and production safety-classifier behavior remain outside automated coverage.
P005/Future You secondary use is now default-off, explicit opt-in, withdrawable, and legacy P005-derived Observer influence is removed unless consent exists.
A visible P004 clear-all control covers module-local transcripts, memory, Observer state, Skill Vault and current-tab BYOK key while preserving other P00 modules.
BYOK keys remain sessionStorage-only, but static ?admin=1 is still not authorization and the safety fallback remains a keyword heuristic.
All five observed third-party GitHub Action references are pinned to full immutable commit SHAs with version comments.
P004 pins xmg2024/nvwa-skill protocol semantics to commit fdb181f0e057e837e15942707b1ea35845850979 instead of mutable @main.
The static frontend remains dependency-light and does not load third-party JavaScript packages from CDNs.
P004 is static, module metadata is explicit, GitHub Actions and NVWA protocol semantics are pinned, and exact-main CI/Pages passed.
Actual output still depends on user-supplied model endpoints, provider behavior and browser CORS/private-network settings.
Exact-main P00 Quality Gate and GitHub Pages deployment both passed after remediation and the gate now includes executable P004 runtime tests.
Main branch remains unprotected and the public repository still lacks an explicit software license/changelog-style release surface.
P004 README documents BYOK, NVWA limitations, privacy opt-in/withdrawal, local-data clearing, runtime tests, memory intent and safety boundaries.
The product UI exposes API diagnostics, local-data inventory and Future You consent state before cross-module import can occur.
A new p004/core.js extracts testable privacy/runtime primitives and executable tests now cover them.
p004/app.js remains approximately 46 KB and still combines Character Studio, rendering, Observer, persistence, memory and admin orchestration.
The repository has README and a live homepage, but GitHub description is null and topics are empty.
LICENSE, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CITATION.cff and CHANGELOG.md were not present at the audited repository baseline and no owner-choice changes were made.

reasons: AI-Ques is already public and this audit found no committed API keys, real user transcripts or private-repository metadata in the reviewed P004 surface.
P004 is explicitly marked as a prototype; public-ok here only means no new recorded publication blocker, not patentability, ownership or legal clearance.

findings.title: Cross-module P005 evidence import lacks explicit opt-in
evidence: p004/core.js defaults p005Observer to false and p004/app.js gates importP005()/collectP005() on CORE.canImportP005(consentState()).
The P004 Data panel exposes an explicit Future You opt-in toggle and withdrawal path.
When consent is absent or withdrawn, P004 rebuilds Observer state from P004-only user messages so legacy P005 influence is not retained.
findings.recommendation: Keep P005 import default-off and retain executable consent regression tests when interoperability changes.

findings.title: Persistent P004 data lacks a unified clear/retention control
evidence: P004 now exposes a visible Data panel with a two-step clear-all action.
The action removes P004 character/thread/memory/observer/active/consent localStorage keys, clears the current-tab BYOK key and deletes the IndexedDB Skill Vault.
The UI explicitly states that P001/P002/P005 and the shared Persona are not deleted.
findings.recommendation: Keep the clear-all scope aligned with any future P004 storage namespace or database additions.

findings.title: Static ?admin=1 research view is not an authorization boundary
evidence: p004/app.js enables adminMode when the URL query parameter admin=1 is present.
p004/index.html labels clinical/status signals admin only while also acknowledging that production requires server-side RBAC.
findings.recommendation: Treat the Pages surface as research-preview/demo only; real admin-only access requires authenticated backend RBAC and server-side field filtering.

findings.title: Safety override is a keyword heuristic, not a production safety agent
evidence: p004/app.js defines a fixed SAFETY_TERMS list and urgentSafety() checks whether any term is contained in user text.
This mechanism cannot reliably cover euphemisms, English/multilingual expressions, negation/context or broader risk semantics.
findings.recommendation: Keep the client keyword path as a fallback, but describe it as best-effort; production should use a dedicated safety classifier/policy layer with evaluated coverage.

findings.title: P004 core behavior is not exercised by automated runtime tests
evidence: tests/p004-runtime.mjs is executable and is run by the P00 Quality Gate.
It exercises consent semantics, creator validation, memory normalization, safety fallback, BYOK success, 401, network failure, temporary test-key restoration and clearDirect lifecycle.
The remediated PR gate and exact-main P00 Quality Gate both passed.
findings.recommendation: Extend runtime coverage with a lightweight browser smoke when a browser-test dependency is justified.

findings.title: Mutable GitHub Action and NVWA references weaken supply-chain reproducibility
evidence: actions/checkout, configure-pages, upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages are pinned to full reviewed commit SHAs in the observed workflows.
P004 app/NVWA contract pins protocolVersion to xmg2024/nvwa-skill@fdb181f0e057e837e15942707b1ea35845850979.
tests/structure.mjs enforces immutable Action refs and the exact expected pins.
findings.recommendation: Advance Action/NVWA pins only through reviewed updates with the full P00 Quality Gate.

findings.title: P004 runtime is concentrated in one large application file
evidence: p004/core.js now extracts storage keys, consent semantics, creator validation, memory normalization and the keyword safety fallback into a testable module.
p004/app.js is still approximately 46 KB and continues to own Character Studio rendering, persistence orchestration, Observer, admin rendering and most memory/chat workflow.
findings.recommendation: Continue incremental extraction of Observer/storage/memory/rendering modules before major new P004 feature growth.

findings.title: Local fallback memory is closer to truncated transcript storage than summarized retrieval memory
evidence: The static BYOK fallback still stores normalized/truncated user text as a durable local memory item when no memory backend is present.
The README describes the intended future summary/salience/retrieval architecture, but the local fallback is not yet that architecture.
findings.recommendation: Either rename the local fallback as prototype memory notes in the UI or add summary/salience/retrieval behavior before stronger long-term-memory claims.

findings.title: Public repository has no explicit software license
evidence: The audited repository root does not contain LICENSE and GitHub metadata reports license=null.
findings.recommendation: Owner should choose and add an appropriate license; repo-auditor must not choose licensing terms automatically.

findings.title: Main branch quality gate is not enforced by branch protection
evidence: GitHub branch metadata for main reports protected=false and required status checks enforcement off.
findings.recommendation: When moving beyond rapid prototype mode, enable a ruleset/branch protection and require the P00 Quality Gate before merge.

limitations: No real OpenAI-compatible, FreeLLMAPI or NVWA backend request was executed as part of this re-audit.
No full browser automation/accessibility/cross-browser test was run; P004 runtime coverage is Node-based for extracted core/API behavior.
The client-side safety fallback is still keyword-based and is not a validated or production-grade safety classifier.
Static ?admin=1 remains a demo/research-preview affordance rather than authenticated authorization.
No claim is made that P004's heuristic personality/clinical inference is psychometrically validated.
Owner-supplied patent, employer/client/PI request, background-IP and ownership questions were not collected in this P004-focused pass.
recheck_triggers: Any change to P004 Observer import or cross-module P005 data reuse.
Any change to BYOK secret handling or arbitrary endpoint support.
Introduction of a real backend/admin authentication layer.
Changes to safety classification or crisis-response behavior.
Changes to NVWA protocol pinning or distillation execution.
Major refactor of p004/app.js or addition of runtime/browser tests.
First formal research data collection or production deployment.
